clue.text: Talk about a stink over fuel!

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for talk is read backwards

parts.note: to rap is to talk or chat

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word for a stink is read backwards

parts.note: niff is British slang for a stink or bad smell

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about a bad smell from a fuel tank.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'about' and 'over' signal reversal here; 'stink' uses the British slang word niff.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is a fuel burned in lamps and heaters, called kerosene in the US.

clue.text: Little horror in a tight spot

definitions.meaning: a mischievous child, a little rascal

explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is both an affectionate name for a naughty child and a fix or predicament.

clue.text: Spin upset half of Tories at end of conference

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upwards, so they read backwards
half of takes the first three of the six letters
end of points to the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Spin doctors upset half the Tories at the close of the party conference.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns letters upwards; 'half of' takes the first half of Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to spin or turn about an axis.

clue.text: Anticipate store being rebuilt in autumn

indicators.note: in places the rebuilt store inside the season word

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: being rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A shop expected to be reconstructed in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rebuilt' is the anagram signal for store; 'autumn' gives the American word for the season, which wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance to prevent something, to anticipate it.

clue.text: Special enclosure in wages exhibits unskilfulness

indicators.note: in places the special and enclosure pieces inside the wages

parts.note: income is the money earned, one's wages
pet as an adjective means special or favourite, as in a pet project
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure on a letter

explanation.surface: A special enclosure in a pay packet shows a lack of skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' looks like it describes the enclosure, but it is the adjective pet, as in pet project; the enclosure is the letter abbreviation enc.
explanation.definitionFit: Incompetence is lack of ability or skill, which is what unskilfulness means.

clue.text: Two dogs, one ball

indicators.note: Two asks for the word for the dogs to be written down twice in a row

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A pair of dogs fighting over a single ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'dogs' is one breed, POM, said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a small decorative ball of wool or threads, as on a woolly hat.

clue.text: US city supports honour with triumphant cry

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means the cry stands below the honour, holding it up

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
aha is a cry of triumph or discovery

explanation.surface: An American city backs an award with a cry of triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, in the United States.

clue.text: Urge single girl to be extravagant

parts.note: to prod is to urge or goad
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
gal is a casual word for a girl

explanation.surface: Encouraging an unmarried young woman to splash out.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, as in the prodigal son of the parable.

clue.text: Period in which one picked up draw, enough for silver bowl

indicators.note: in which tells us the next piece goes inside the period

parts.note: a month is a period of time

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue lifts the letters so they read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: During a month one team earned a draw, enough to win a silver trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses the draw word, as letters in a down light read upwards; 'one' and 'enough for' only join the surface about a team winning a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A monteith is a large ornamental punch bowl, usually silver, with a notched rim.

clue.text: It's such a downpour we can't see through it

definitions.text: It's such a downpour we can't see through it

parts.words: It's such a downpour we can't see through it
parts.note: reads as torrential rain blocking the view, but means both a great waterfall and the clouding of the eye's lens that blocks sight

explanation.walkthrough: The 'downpour' is a large waterfall; the same word names an eye condition in which a clouded lens stops the sufferer seeing through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall and also an opacity of the eye's lens that impairs vision.

clue.text: Strange old Roman — one that can make a report

definitions.text: one that can make a report

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd ancient Roman turns out to be a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' scrambles O and ROMAN. The 'report' is a bang, not a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A maroon is a firework or distress rocket that explodes with a loud bang, a report.

clue.text: Insect found in scary part of Sussex, say

parts.note: creepy means scary or eerie

indicators.note: say tells us the town is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Crawley is a town in West Sussex, England

explanation.surface: An insect turns up in a frightening corner of southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAWLY is heard as CRAWLEY, a West Sussex town near Gatwick airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A creepy-crawly is an informal term for an insect, spider or other small crawling creature.

clue.text: Plant seen in great numbers around university

indicators.note: around tells us the word for great numbers goes round the university letter

parts.note: lots means great numbers, as in lots of people

explanation.surface: A plant that grows in profusion across a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant, a type of lily sacred in several Asian religions.

clue.text: Seagoing soldier consuming fish spread

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the soldier takes the fish inside him

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A Royal Marine eating fish with a buttery spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seagoing soldier' is the standard crossword route to a marine; the gar is a needle-nosed fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute spread on bread.

clue.text: Cook suitably tangy pastry dish

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
well means suitably or properly
tart means sharp-tasting or tangy

explanation.surface: Instructions to cook a sharp-tasting pastry dish properly.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bakewell tart is an English pastry with jam and almond filling, named after a Derbyshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bakewell tart is a shortcrust pastry case filled with jam and almond sponge.

clue.text: It's most unlike Solomon, at any rate

parts.note: least is the opposite of most, so this asks for the least of a quality
King Solomon is the biblical byword for wisdom, so his name stands for wise

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is the very opposite of the wise King Solomon, at any rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Least wise is the opposite of Solomon, famous for wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an informal word for at least or at any rate.

clue.text: Biased pair imbibing a herbal infusion out East

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the pair takes in the a
out means the letter for East is removed

parts.note: a tisane is a herbal tea or infusion

explanation.surface: A one-sided couple drinking herbal tea in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' tells us to drop the compass letter from the infusion, not to look eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisan means strongly biased in favour of one side.

clue.text: Brief stay to check deliveries

parts.note: to check is to stop or halt
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A short visit to inspect parcels and post.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls (deliveries) bowled in a row by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a brief stay at a place in the course of a journey.

clue.text: Shoot unknown male in Irish islands? He might

indicators.note: in places the shoot, unknown and male pieces inside the islands

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland
a tiller is a shoot sprouting from the base of a plant
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Asking whether to fire at an unidentified man on the islands off Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He might' completes the clue: he might shoot. As wordplay, though, 'Shoot' is a plant's tiller, not firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunner in the artillery is one who might shoot, the definition pointing back to the clue's first word.

clue.text: Knight in armour goes to a foreign city

indicators.note: in places the knight letter inside the armour

parts.note: mail is chain armour
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight in armour travels to an overseas city.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside MAIL gives MANIL, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is the capital city of the Philippines.

clue.text: Old club that's provided vegetable preparation for starter

indicators.note: for starter means the vegetable preparation comes first, before that's

parts.note: mash is mashed potato, a prepared vegetable
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something that served mashed potato as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: A mashie is an old name for a golf club roughly equal to a five iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie was an old iron golf club, used for lofted shots.

clue.text: High-speed rap artist?

parts.note: suggests a rapper who delivers lyrics very fast, but describes a performer whose feet rap out a quick beat on the floor

explanation.walkthrough: The 'rap' is the tapping of metal-tipped shoes, not rap music.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-dancer's shoes rap rapidly on the floor, making them a rap artist of a kind.

clue.text: Thallophytes, in original Gaelic

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Simple plants named in the ancient Irish language.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across originAL GAElic.
explanation.definitionFit: Thallophytes are simple plants without stems or leaves, and algae are the chief example.

clue.text: Headdress originally introduced in seat of Irish kings

indicators.note: in places the first letter of introduced inside the seat of kings

parts.note: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of the High Kings of Ireland

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A crown first brought into the ancient royal seat of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headdress or coronet.

clue.text: Scholar loses books, say, about primitive man

indicators.note: loses means the scholar drops the letters for books

parts.note: a savant is a learned person or scholar
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation for say is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, that is, say

explanation.surface: An academic, short of books, perhaps writes about early man.
explanation.walkthrough: SAVANT without NT leaves SAVA; 'about' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A savage, in old usage, is an uncivilised or primitive person.

clue.text: Beastly about area, like a country youth

indicators.note: about means the word for beastly goes around the area letter

parts.note: swinish means beastly, like a pig

explanation.surface: A rough country lad behaves boorishly about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like the definition but supplies the pig-like word that goes round the area letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a country youth or rustic lover, so swainish means like one.

clue.text: Looks after dogfish

definitions.meaning: cares for, tends, as one tends the sick
nurse hounds and nurse sharks are kinds of dogfish

explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to care for someone; a nurse is also a name for a type of dogfish or shark.

clue.text: Watch sounds similar to wash

indicators.note: sounds tells us the word for similar is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: like means similar
a wake is the wash left behind a moving boat

explanation.surface: A timepiece that sounds much like one swirling in water.
explanation.walkthrough: LYKE is heard as LIKE. A lykewake is a northern English and Scottish term for a night watch kept over a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A lykewake is a vigil or watch kept over a corpse before burial.
